previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and chronic tracheostomy was admitted for increased greenish tracheal secretions with blood streaks, dyspnea on exertion, chills, and odynophagia. She had multiple recent admissions with similar symptoms, none of which showed infection. Initial evaluation revealed normal vital signs, clear lungs, and a chest X-ray without acute findings. Blood cultures were negative, and early sputum samples were contaminated. A tracheal aspirate on hospital day three confirmed Staphylococcus aureus and Haemophilus influenzae, leading to a diagnosis of bacterial tracheitis. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin, which was continued at home for a full 10-day course. Her chronic pain, microcytic anemia, and GERD were managed with home medications. She improved clinically, was discharged home with visiting nurse support, and had follow-up arranged with her primary care provider and ENT.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You came in because you were having increased sputum, tracheal 
pain,  and chills. We were worried that may have had an 
infection in your tracheostomy. We treated you with IV 
antibiotics while you were here. 

Your symptoms improved and we now feel that you are well enough 
to go home. You will need to take antibiotics for 9 days. We are 
sending you home on an antibiotic called doxycycline. You should 
take one pill per day for 10 more doses. We are also giving you 
a medication for your nausea called Zofran. Please take Zofran 
15 minutes before taking doxycycline.

You will see an infectious disease doctor and lung doctor for 
further treatment.

If you develop fevers, difficulty breathing, chest pain or 
increased pain around your trachea, please call Dr. ___ 
or go to the emergency room.

It was a pleasure taking care of you, and we are happy that you 
are feeling better!
